paragraphs.text: When I asked my mother whether she wanted the piano sold, she stayed silent and pulled the cover over its keys. I took that as a refusal and canceled the buyer's visit. That evening she asked me to move the framed photographs back onto the lid.

I mistook my mother's silence for agreement until she slid her hearing aid across the table and pointed to its empty battery compartment. We had been discussing a phone call she had not heard. I wrote the caller's name and request on the back of the envelope, and she answered each point in writing.

When the referee announced the result, the coach looked first at the score sheet and then at the floor. A pause entered the hall, holding the explanation in the shape of its own duration. The hall settled around the pause, and in that settled quality the full story of the defeat became apparent.
Ivo laid a folded map beside the chessboard and placed a pebble on one corner. The quiet turned crowded. He had marked the footpaths in blue pencil and the wells in brown.
